question: A nucleus $P$ has mass number $A$, while another nucleus $Q$ has mass number $8A$. Without using numerical values of $R_0$, find how many times the radius and surface area of $Q$ are compared to those of $P$.

options.A: Radius of $Q$ is $8$ times and surface area is $64$ times that of $P$.
options.B: Radius of $Q$ is $4$ times and surface area is $16$ times that of $P$.
options.C: Radius and surface area of $Q$ are both twice those of $P$.
options.D: $\dfrac{R_Q}{R_P}=\left(\dfrac{8A}{A}\right)^{1/3}=2$. Since surface area $S\propto R^2$, $\dfrac{S_Q}{S_P}=2^2=4$. Thus radius is $2$ times and surface area is $4$ times.
